Fetch boxing events from BoxingBook API with enhanced data extraction

Source: R/fetch_boxingbook_events.R
fetch_boxingbook_events.Rd

Retrieves a list of boxing events from the BoxingBook API and automatically extracts and cleans the nested distribution data into separate data frames. This function provides access to comprehensive event data including dates, venues, promoters, and detailed statistics.

Usage

fetch_boxingbook_events(
  page = 0,
  page_size = 50,
  sort = "date,id,DESC",
  date_from = NULL,
  date_to = NULL,
  promoter = NULL,
  venue = NULL,
  timeout = 30,
  extract_distributions = TRUE,
  assign_global = FALSE
)

Arguments

page

Integer. Page number for pagination (default: 0).

page_size

Integer. Number of records per page, max 100 (default: 50).

sort

Character. Sorting criteria in format "field1,field2,ORDER" where ORDER is ASC or DESC (default: "date,id,DESC").

date_from

Character. Filter events from this date in YYYY-MM-DD format (optional).

date_to

Character. Filter events to this date in YYYY-MM-DD format (optional).

promoter

Character. Filter by promoter name (optional).

venue

Character. Filter by venue name (optional).

timeout

Numeric. Request timeout in seconds (default: 30).

extract_distributions

Logical. Whether to extract distribution data into separate data frames (default: TRUE).

assign_global

Logical. Whether to assign extracted data frames to global environment (default: FALSE).

Value

A list containing:

  • events: Main events data frame with core event information

  • gender_distribution: Gender distribution data (if extracted)

  • result_distribution: Fight result distribution data (if extracted)

  • country_distribution: Country distribution data (if extracted)

  • weight_distribution: Weight class distribution data (if extracted)

Details

The function connects to the BoxingBook API to retrieve event data and automatically cleans the complex nested structure. When extract_distributions = TRUE, the function separates distribution statistics into clean, analyzable data frames.

If assign_global = TRUE, the following objects are assigned to the global environment:

  • boxingbook_events: Main events data

  • boxingbook_gender_dist: Gender distribution data

  • boxingbook_result_dist: Result distribution data

  • boxingbook_country_dist: Country distribution data

  • boxingbook_weight_dist: Weight distribution data

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Basic usage with data extraction
data <- fetch_boxingbook_events()
events <- data$events
gender_stats <- data$gender_distribution

# Assign to global environment
fetch_boxingbook_events(assign_global = TRUE)
# Now you can access: boxingbook_events, boxingbook_gender_dist, etc.

# Get events with filters and extract distributions
aus_events <- fetch_boxingbook_events(
  date_from = "2024-01-01",
  extract_distributions = TRUE
)
} # }
